thread.title: Senate Passes Legislation to Roll Back Appliance Energy Conservation Rules
thread.title_full: Senate Passes Legislation to Roll Back Appliance Energy Conservation Rules

author: Jim Mishler
title: Senate Passes Legislation to Roll Back Appliance Energy Conservation Rules
text:
• Legislation to roll back Biden-era appliance energy conservation rules cleared the Senate on April 30, 2025.
• The measure was introduced by Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, who recently assumed his Senate seat.
• The bill has already been approved in the House and will be sent to President Donald Trump for his signature.
• Husted stated that the bill eliminates unnecessary regulations on home appliances that do not benefit Americans.
• He claimed the legislation will impact both manufacturers and consumers positively.
• Husted emphasized that the bill aims to reduce red tape, restore consumer choice, and lower costs for Americans.
• Senate Majority Leader John Thune criticized the Biden administration's regulations, claiming they cost Americans $1.8 trillion.
• Thune expressed that the new legislation reflects a shift towards less government intrusion in the marketplace.
• The legislation covers 20 household and commercial products, including dishwashers, air conditioning units, and washing machines.
• The Public Interest Research Group argued that the previous rules should be supported, estimating savings of $107 per household annually over the next two decades.
